question: What is the general percentage range of daily calories suggested by standard protein guidelines?
explanation: Standard dietary guidelines recommend that protein make up between 10 and 35 percent of an adult's total daily caloric intake. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T003#GNS227_U6_T003_h1)

question: Why do modern clinical nurses encounter high protein diets more frequently than in the past?

options.A: Hospitals banned carbohydrates entirely from clinical meal trays
options.B: Patients use them widely for weight loss and muscle preservation
options.C: Standard dietary guidelines now demand excessive protein intake
options.D: Government mandates require all citizens to consume extra meat

explanation: Widespread public interest in weight management and fitness has driven patients to adopt high protein regimens independently. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T003#GNS227_U6_T003_h1)

question: Which specific plasma protein plays the primary role in maintaining oncotic pressure and fluid balance?
explanation: Albumin is the major plasma protein responsible for maintaining intravascular oncotic pressure and keeping fluid inside blood vessels. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T003#GNS227_U6_T003_h2)

question: A patient with a severe protein deficiency is most at risk for developing which clinical sign?
explanation: Low blood protein levels drop oncotic pressure, allowing fluid to leak out of capillaries into surrounding tissues to cause edema. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T003#GNS227_U6_T003_h2)

question: What metabolic state characterizes patients with severe burns or major physical trauma?
explanation: Severe physical trauma triggers rapid tissue breakdown, causing the body to excrete more nitrogen than it takes in. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T003#GNS227_U6_T003_h3)

question: Why is a high protein diet specifically ordered for a patient with deep pressure ulcers?

options.A: Proteins completely replace the need for sterile wound dressings
options.B: Extra protein acts as a mild topical antiseptic over the ulcer bed
options.C: High protein intake stops bacterial colonization in chronic skin wounds
options.D: Amino acids are required to synthesize new granulation tissue and heal wounds

explanation: Wound healing demands a high supply of building blocks for cell division and collagen synthesis, which extra dietary protein provides. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T003#GNS227_U6_T003_h3)

question: What defines a complete dietary protein source?

options.A: It requires no digestion in the stomach
options.B: It comes exclusively from plant-based foods
options.C: It has zero calories and zero fat content
options.D: It contains all nine essential amino acids

explanation: A complete protein supplies every single one of the essential amino acids that the human body cannot manufacture independently. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T003#GNS227_U6_T003_h4)

question: How can a patient following a strict plant-based diet ensure adequate essential amino acid intake?

options.A: Avoiding all forms of soy and legume products entirely
options.B: Consuming a variety of complementary plant proteins over the course of the day
options.C: Taking high-dose iron supplements with every single meal
options.D: Eating only raw green vegetables and drinking distilled water

explanation: Since individual plant foods may lack certain amino acids, mixing different plant sources ensures the body receives all necessary building blocks. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T003#GNS227_U6_T003_h4)

question: What is the standard baseline RDA for protein in a healthy sedentary adult?
explanation: The baseline recommended dietary allowance for healthy, non-athletic adults sits at 0.8 grams per kilogram of body weight daily. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T003#GNS227_U6_T003_h5)

question: Which lab marker should a nurse interpret cautiously when assessing nutrition in an acutely inflamed patient?
explanation: Albumin acts as a negative acute-phase reactant, meaning its blood levels drop during active inflammation regardless of true nutritional status. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T003#GNS227_U6_T003_h5)

question: What is a practical strategy for a nurse to help a patient who struggles to finish large high-protein meals?

options.A: Provide smaller, frequent protein-rich snacks throughout the day
options.B: Remove all solid food and rely entirely on water intake
options.C: Scold the patient for showing poor compliance with the diet
options.D: Force the patient to finish every bite before leaving the room

explanation: Dividing high-protein foods into smaller, frequent portions prevents the patient from feeling overwhelmed by large meals and improves total daily intake. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T003#GNS227_U6_T003_h6)

question: A patient on a high protein regimen begins refusing water because they feel full. What is the most appropriate nursing action?

options.A: Explain that extra protein intake requires increased fluid to protect kidney function
options.B: Document that the patient refuses to cooperate with basic ward routines
options.C: Withhold all further protein supplements until fluid intake normalizes completely
options.D: Replace all drinking water with thick sugary juices to boost calories

explanation: Higher protein loads increase metabolic waste products that require adequate renal clearance, making proper hydration essential. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T003#GNS227_U6_T003_h6)

question: Which organ system faces the primary workload increase when processing a chronic excess of dietary protein?
explanation: The kidneys filter and excrete nitrogenous waste products resulting from protein metabolism, bearing the brunt of excess intake. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T003#GNS227_U6_T003_h7)

question: Why might a patient following an unmonitored high-protein, low-carbohydrate diet develop frequent constipation?

options.A: Severe restriction of carbohydrate-rich foods typically reduces daily dietary fiber intake
options.B: High protein diets completely shut down large bowel motility permanently
options.C: Proteins absorb all available water in the stomach before digestion begins
options.D: Excess protein coats the intestinal walls and stops normal peristalsis

explanation: Cutting out grains, fruits, and starchy vegetables often eliminates the primary sources of dietary fiber needed for regular bowel movements. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T003#GNS227_U6_T003_h7)
